extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners seeking to use the USPTO Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for entering and prosecuting a U.S. patent application under the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) at the USPTO, including eligibility, document submission, timing, translations, IDS obligations, and prosecution practice effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and benefits of PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) is a framework in which an application whose claims have been determined to be patentable by an Office of Earlier Examination (OEE) is eligible to go through an accelerated examination in an Office of Later Examination (OLE) with a simple procedure upon an applicant’s request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH exploits search/examination information of the OEE to (1) deliver lower prosecution costs, (2) support applicants in obtaining stable patent rights efficiently worldwide, and (3) reduce search/examination burden and improve examination quality in major patent offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH eligibility requirements (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your USPTO patent application is eligible for PPH if (1) you have received an indication of allowable subject matter in a related application from a partnering PPH office; (2) the application with the indication of allowable subject matter and your USPTO application share a common earliest priority date; and (3) examination has not begun on your USPTO patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm partnering office membership (links provided). All three conditions must be met before requesting PPH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications filed before PPH program start
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed before the starting date of the PPH program is eligible for participation as long as the other criteria are met (see eligibility requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date before program start does not alone disqualify; still must satisfy the three-part eligibility test.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH participating offices list and portal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to find a complete listing of PPH participating countries: USPTO PPH webpage and a one-stop PPH information portal hosted on the JPO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portal (JPO) includes up-to-date statistics and fillable request forms; USPTO page lists partnering offices. Use these resources to verify partner status and obtain forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to enter PPH at USPTO (PPH Request Form requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To have your application considered for PPH you must meet all the criteria and submit a PPH Request Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO provides a list of PPH Request forms. Ensure all eligibility conditions are met before submission; include required accompanying documents (IDS, translations, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web document descriptions for PPH filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific document description strings to use when submitting PPH-related documents via EFS-Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Petition to make special under Patent Pros Hwy.' for the PPH request; use 'Information Disclosure Statement (IDS)' for IDS; use 'Preliminary amendment' for any preliminary amendment accompanying the PPH request. Using correct document descriptions helps proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: OEE work product retrieval via Dossier Access / PATENTSCOPE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copy of the office action from the OEE application is available via the Dossier Access System, applicant may request that the USPTO obtain the copy via that system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should check Dossier Access and WIPO PATENTSCOPE to determine availability. If dossier access is limited to offices (not public), or applicant cannot determine availability, provide a copy of the OEE work product. To avoid dismissal of the initial PPH request and potential denial of participation, verify that the document is actually available via the Dossier Access System or PATENTSCOPE before requesting retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirements for OEE work product
rubrics_metrics.description: If an English translation of the OEE work product is required, the English translation may be a machine translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPTO finds a machine translation of such poor quality that it is difficult to understand, the applicant may be required to submit a manual translation. The manual translation does not need to be certified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'examination has not begun' (substantive examination timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement that examination of the US application must not have begun refers to substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities-only actions (e.g., Notice to File Missing Parts) are not substantive examination. A restriction requirement does not necessarily start substantive examination; a PPH petition may still be filed if the examiner has not started on the first action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination still required under PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination under the PPH is conducted according to US law and guidelines in the same way as non-PPH applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH does not guarantee that USPTO results will match OEE results. Empirically, PPH applications generally have higher allowance rates, fewer office actions per disposal, reduced RCE filing rates, and reduced appeal rates than non-PPH applications, but allowance is not automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of continuations and divisionals based on OEE allowable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. continuation/divisional application may be eligible to participate in the PPH program based on the allowable claims from the OEE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you file a continuation/divisional, you may use the OEE allowable claims as the basis for PPH for the new U.S. application, subject to meeting other eligibility criteria (priority date, examination not begun, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national stage timing and filing-number guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When entering the U.S. national stage of a PCT application, there is no requirement to file the PPH request simultaneously with the national stage entry papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested to wait until you have your U.S. application number so you can identify it on the PPH request. Note that the filing date of a national stage entry into the U.S. of a PCT application is the international filing date (35 U.S.C. 363).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH processing timelines and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH program does not have a 12‑month final disposition goal like the Accelerated Examination (AE) program and does not expedite pre-exam processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the PPH request is filed, the PPH request is generally decided within 4 months from filing. If granted, the examiner will generally examine the application within 2–3 months from grant of the PPH request provided the application has completed all pre-exam processing and is ready for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to submit IDS for references cited in OEE work product
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the first action in the OEE application is a first action allowance that cites several references, an IDS listing those references should be submitted when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although submission of an IDS in that scenario is not an explicit PPH requirement, applicants have a duty to bring to the Office any material prior art or other information cited or brought to applicant's attention in any related foreign application. See MPEP 2001.06(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS requirements for foreign-language documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS must comply with content requirements of 37 CFR 1.98; when documents are not in English you must submit a concise explanation of relevance pursuant to 37 CFR 1.98(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a non-English document was cited in a search report or action by a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application, the concise explanation requirement can be satisfied by submitting an English-language version of the search report or action which indicates the degree of relevance found by the foreign office (see MPEP 609.04(a), subsection III.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment availability in PPH applications
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA (Patent Term Adjustment) is available to applications accepted in the PPH program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance into PPH does not forfeit PTA rights; PTA calculations continue to apply per USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time during PPH prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available for applications accepted in the PPH program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may obtain statutory extensions of time during prosecution of a US application in the PPH program consistent with 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting a deficient PPH request
rubrics_metrics.description: If errors are found on a filed PPH request, a corrected PPH request form should be submitted via EFS-Web as soon as possible if no decision has been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the corrected form plus a transmittal letter explaining the correction. If a decision on the PPH request has already been received, submit the corrected PPH request form in your reply to the PPH decision with a transmittal letter explaining the errors being corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of utility model or innovation patent OEE work product
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally you cannot rely on allowed claims from a utility model or an innovation patent from an OEE to request PPH in the USPTO, with one exception for Korean utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models/innovation patents typically are not required to meet the same patentability standards as regular utility patents and often are not subject to substantive examination. USPTO has made an exception for Korean utility models (see USPTO notice); other practices remain under consideration but no general inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive Extended European Search Report (EESR) as a basis for PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: A positive EESR means that the EPO generated an EESR prior to an office action and the EESR only contains 'A' references (no 'X' or 'Y') directed to a particular claim, so that claim is considered allowable by the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use that EPO allowable claim as the basis for a PPH request in the US application. All the claims in the US application must sufficiently correspond to that EP allowable claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim correspondence and amendment rules for 'sufficiently correspond'
rubrics_metrics.description: US claims will be considered to sufficiently correspond with the claims allowed by the OEE if the US claims are of the same or similar scope or the US claims are narrower in scope than the allowed claims; the additional limitation that makes the US claims narrower must be presented in dependent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the narrower dependent claim is indicated as being allowable if written in independent form, you may rewrite the allowable dependent claim in independent form. An independent claim rejected by the US examiner may be amended to include a limitation previously presented in a dependent claim indicated as having allowable subject matter; such an amendment can meet the sufficient correspondence requirement only if that limitation was previously presented in a dependent claim indicated as allowable but objected to only because it depended on a rejected claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice in PPH applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Although MPEP 708.02(a), section III describes telephonic restriction practice in applications made special for examination, applications made special for health/age and PPH are not subject to this telephonic restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, it is permissible for an applicant to request a written restriction letter in a PPH application.
